subject: squirrels
one_liner: On-demand nut delivery to a hole you almost remember digging.
brand_voice_notes: Logistics-brochure deadpan. The company treats instinct as an inefficiency and memory loss as churn. Prices are confident, apologies are absent, and every metric is presented as good news.

hero.h1: Winter is a supply chain problem.
hero.sub: Cache delivers foraged, grade-A nuts to any branch, stump, or shallow hole in under 40 minutes. Stop climbing. Start allocating.

features.title: Last-Branch Delivery
features.blurb: A background-checked adult climbs your tree and leaves the order at the drey entrance. No contact, no eye contact, per your saved preferences.

features.title: Burial-as-a-Service
features.blurb: Your Dasher buries surplus acorns in GPS-logged locations you will never visit. The memory game is over. We won it for you.

features.title: Hawk Surge Pricing
features.blurb: Delivery fees adjust in real time to local raptor activity. When coverage gets dangerous, it costs more. This is fair to everyone except you.

pricing_tiers.name: Forager
pricing_tiers.tagline: You keep gathering your own nuts. We keep the app open.
perks: One free delivery to a hole of our choosing

pricing_tiers.name: Hoarder
pricing_tiers.tagline: For the squirrel who has stopped pretending this is about winter.
perks: Free delivery on orders over 200 acorns

pricing_tiers.name: Apex Rodent
perks: Guaranteed winter reserve, or we mail you a letter
Surge immunity below Category 2 hawk activity

testimonials.quote: I buried 3,000 acorns last season and found 200. This year a man named Doug buried them for me and I found zero, but the app says they're safe.
testimonials.name: Pretzel
testimonials.title: Eastern Gray, Cache Portfolio Manager, Prospect Park

testimonials.quote: The hawk surcharge felt punitive until I remembered what it pays for. Now I tip 30% and stay indoors.
testimonials.name: Walnut
testimonials.title: Fox Squirrel, HOA Liaison, Oak Cluster 4

testimonials.quote: Cache didn't change what I eat. It changed how far I'm willing to walk, which is now nothing.
testimonials.name: Gary
testimonials.title: American Red, Early Adopter, Third Feeder on the Left

demo_screen_concept: A live order-tracking screen: a stylized backyard map with a dashed courier route from BIG OAK FULFILLMENT to the customer's drey, a Dasher marker (Doug, on branch 3 of 7) advancing along it, a status timeline (Order confirmed, Nuts inspected, Doug is climbing, Delivered to hole), an ETA chip with the current hawk-surge multiplier, a tip slider denominated in acorns, and a My Caches sidebar listing buried inventory with 47% flagged LOCATION FORGOTTEN.

design_direction.style: Glossy consumer super-app marketplace, harvest daylight mode. The page is staged as the consumer site of a heavily funded on-demand logistics company that has decided the squirrel is a lapsed customer with a fulfillment problem and prices instinct by the delivery. A warm cashew-cream ground (#FDF8EF) carries big rounded marketplace cards: 20px radii, flat warm fills one shade off the ground, a single soft diffuse shadow (0 10px 30px at low alpha, no second shadow, no inner highlight), pill-shaped CTAs and chips everywhere, and a sticky cream top nav with a pill order button, so the page reads like a delivery app that floated onto the web rather than a website. The core motif is the cache pin: an acorn-shaped map pin drawn in CSS/SVG that drops into the hero, anchors dashed courier routes (2px dashed lines with animated dash offset, marching like a live route) arcing between sections, and shrinks into list bullets and status dots. Floating UI chips do the annotation: rounded ETA chips (ETA 38 MIN), status chips (DOUG IS CLIMBING), and surge chips (HAWK SURGE 1.4x) sit overlapped on photo cards and section corners like escaped app components. One burnt squirrel-fur orange (#D9530B) carries the wordmark, every primary CTA, the live order dot, and the highlighted word per headline; one rationed oak-leaf green (#2F6B3A) handles delivered states, verified badges, and tip confirmations, and appears nowhere else. Gabarito sets the wordmark and headlines in chunky rounded geometric caps with app-store confidence; Figtree carries plain, faintly ops-review body copy. Every figure that pretends to be fulfillment telemetry (ETA minutes, acorn counts, surge multipliers, tier prices, forgotten-cache percentages) is set in IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures inside inset cream wells, so it reads like the order screen, not marketing. Motion is courier-restrained: the cache pin drops once on load with a single small bounce, dashed routes march at 1px/frame, cards lift 3px on hover with the shadow softening, CTAs depress 1px on press, the ETA chip ticks down once on reveal, sections fade up 6px on scroll with a 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No dark mode, no glass, no blur panels, no clay dual shadows, no offset brutalist shadows, no engraving or certificate rules, no signage grids, no neon glow, no serifs, no emoji. Reads like a company that files object permanence under 'retention risk' and considers the oak tree an unlicensed competitor.
design_direction.archetype: consumer on-demand delivery marketplace landing, app-first split hero
design_direction.motion_vocab: single pin-drop bounce on load, marching dashed routes, 3px card lifts, 1px CTA depress, one ETA tick on reveal, 6px scroll fade-ups with 40ms stagger, all behind prefers-reduced-motion
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Split hero on cream: left column carries the headline stack (one orange-highlighted word), sub, pill CTA, and a deadpan app-badge row; right column is a large 20px-radius photo card of the customer (hero.webp if present, otherwise a CSS acorn-pin illustration) with three floating UI chips overlapped on its edges: an ETA chip, a DOUG IS CLIMBING status chip, and an acorn tip chip. A dashed courier route arcs from the nav's order pill down into the photo card's cache pin.
